document_title: Applied Optoelectronics says power is one reason its 2027 expansion will take longer

1.hook: Built for light, waiting on power
1.dek: A Sugar Land maker of data center optics says its 2027 expansion plan in the United States will take longer. It cites a longer than expected wait for electrical power, among other construction issues. The bay is drawn to illustrate.

2.dek: The company makes optical transceivers for internet and AI data centers. Its chief executive says the company believes demand for AI-related optical technologies is accelerating. The module is drawn to illustrate.

3.hook: Laser chips, made only in Sugar Land
3.dek: The quarterly report puts the laser design team there too. The company also leases about 209,665 square feet on Gillingham Lane in Sugar Land, used mainly for manufacturing. The plant is drawn to its stated floor area, not its shape.

4.hook: The biggest building is not built yet
4.dek: The company has leased two Houston buildings on Chimney Rock Road that are still to be built. Together they come to about 1,093,807 rentable square feet. Each property is drawn as a square of its stated floor area.
labels: Chimney Rock, to be built, 356,186 sq ft
Chimney Rock, to be built, 737,621 sq ft

5.hook: Half the floor by year end
5.dek: The company expects equipment for over 500,000 pieces of 800G and 1.6 Tb products a month by the end of 2026, and over 1 million by the end of 2027. Each pad is an equal share.

6.hook: One stake for each month of work
6.dek: The company entered into leases for the two Chimney Rock Road buildings on August 31st. The quarterly report anticipates substantial completion about 16 months later. The site is drawn to illustrate.

7.hook: The wait, in its own words
7.dek: The chief financial officer, in the November 5th results release. The transformer is drawn to illustrate and stands for no named site or utility.

8.dek: The chief executive says the company recently secured a multi-year strategic agreement with a Tier 1 hyperscale data center customer. The hall is drawn to illustrate.

9.hook: A 2027 target, a wait for power
9.dek: The same November 5th release expects capacity for over 1 million transceivers a month by the end of 2027. The release and the quarterly report are both on file with the SEC.
